t: Section 15 of the Act of July 29, 1892 (27 Stat. 325; 40 U.S.C. 101; D.C. Code 4–120, 22–3111), is amended by deleting “shall, upon conviction thereof, be fined not more than $50.”, and inserting in lieu thereof: “shall be fined not more than $500, or imprisoned not more than six months, or both.”

fable.w: This section only amends a criminal penalty provision, raising the maximum fine from $50 to $500 and adding possible imprisonment of up to six months. There is no tempting reading here: it contains no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Nothing in the text is on-topic for participation.

qwen_block.w: This section amends the criminal penalties for a specific offense, increasing the fine and adding imprisonment. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by non-federal parties in a federal decision-making process. It is purely a substantive change to statutory penalties.
